name: biomanufacturing
title: Biomanufacturing of styrene, one DBTL turn
source: "Workflow 1: Biomanufacturing of Styrene" (PDF, dbtlhub/biomanufacturing/examples), 15 listed activities (10 design, 3 build, 2 test, 2 learn, the PDF's own headings), with tool names from that document; stage structure cross-checked against the BioHackathon26 deck "BH DBTLHub Biomanfacturing case Workflows". Instruments, units and id patterns come from our profile framework/contracts/profiles/biomanufacturing.json, which describes a different case (pinocembrin).
description:
One turn of the cycle for microbial production of styrene, from chassis and
pathway choice to a model that proposes the next strains. The steps follow
the styrene workflow document, which is a list of activities and tools, not
a record of a measured run: it gives no counts, timings or manual work.
Where a step is a person's work it is marked as inferred, to be confirmed
with the lab. The styrene workflow and our profile describe different
cases: the profile is the SYNBIOCHEM pinocembrin pipeline (Carbonell et al.,
Commun Biol 2018; mg/L, UPLC-MS/MS MRM, Sanger, Hamilton STAR). Its units
carry over as contract quantities; its instruments are not asserted for
styrene.

steps.name: Select chassis and retrieve its metabolic model
steps.note: Fixes the host before anything else. The chassis must be recorded with a strain-collection identifier or a construct cannot be compared across cycles (`dbtl:Chassis` in the profile). Tool named in the source: BiGG Models.

steps.name: Predict and reconstruct candidate pathways
steps.note: Covers the source's pathway prediction and enumeration steps (RetroPath2.0, RP2Paths, rpCompletion). Reactions should carry MetaNetX or Rhea accessions, which is what the profile's `accession` pattern accepts.

steps.name: Rank pathways by flux and thermodynamics
steps.note: FBA, thermodynamics and pathway scoring (rpFBA, rpThermo, rpRank, COBRApy). The predicted flux is the number the Learn phase will later be held to, so it needs a unit now.

steps.name: Select enzymes and homologs for each reaction
steps.note: Selenzyme and EnzymeMiner in the source. UniProt accessions are the profile's reference form.

steps.name: Choose engineering targets and regulatory parts
steps.note: Merges two source activities: gene deletion or overexpression targets (OptFlux) and promoter and RBS selection (PartsGenie, RBS Calculator).

steps.name: Design the combinatorial experiment
steps.note: OptDoE in the source. The size limit on the library has to be stated before the design exists. For scale only, and from a different case: the pinocembrin crate on disk compresses 2592 combinations to 16 constructs. No styrene library size is given, so none is recorded here.

steps.name: Design DNA constructs and assembly strategy
steps.note: DNA Weaver, rpBASICDesign and AssemblX in the source. This is the construct specification that crosses the first handover: identifier, parts with registry accessions, chassis, and plate and well.
manual_parts: review of the design before it is released (inferred, not stated in source)

steps.name: Design the cultivation experiment
steps.note: Conditions, factors and biological replicates (OptDoE). Without the replicate count in the package the Test side cannot say whether a titre is a measurement or a single colony.

steps.name: Generate the robot assembly protocol
steps.note: DNA-BOT in the source translates designs into liquid-handler instructions. The robot and its worklist format are not named for styrene, so none is asserted here.

steps.name: Assemble the constructs
steps.note: Not a separate item in the source, which lists protocol generation and then verification; the assembly run sits between them. Losses here are where attrition happens in practice, and nothing in the source counts them.
manual_parts: loading reagents and plates onto the deck (inferred, not stated in source)
transformation into the chassis (inferred, not stated in source)

steps.name: Verify constructs against expected sequence
steps.note: Sequencing results are compared with the designed sequences (TraceTrack in the source). The profile requires `sequence_verified` as a pass/fail at the next handover.

steps.name: Register strains and samples
steps.note: eLabFTW in the source. Ties each strain to its genetic modifications and to the samples made from it, so a later titre can be traced back to a construct. The profile also asks for biomass (OD600) at this handover.

steps.name: Culture strains and measure growth
steps.note: Growth curves give rates and show whether styrene is toxic to the host (omniplate in the source). Biomass is the basis a titre is normalised against.
manual_parts: inoculation and sampling (inferred, not stated in source)

steps.name: Quantify styrene and substrate by chromatography
steps.note: The source names OpenChrom and generic chromatographic measurements. The profile's mg/L titre against a calibration curve is the contract unit; the UPLC-MS/MS method in the profile belongs to the pinocembrin case.

steps.name: Calculate titre, yield and productivity
steps.note: R or Python for derived metrics in the source. A reading below the limit of quantification must say so rather than appear as a small titre.

steps.name: Find metabolic bottlenecks
steps.note: Experimental results are compared with the model's predictions to find where precursor supply or pathway flux limits production (CellNetAnalyzer, COBRApy in the source).

steps.name: Train models and propose the next strains
steps.note: Regression on designs, conditions and production data, then prediction for untested strains (scikit-learn, OptDoE). The profile requires the predicted titre in mg/L with uncertainty, so the next round can be scored against it. The source describes this step but records no run of it.
